partners.diseaseBName: facial palsy, congenital, with ptosis and velopharyngeal dysfunction
partners.mechanism_chain: TUBA1A (HGNC:11677) —DISRUPTS→ Tubulin polymerization (GO:0007032); TUBB6 (HGNC:12240) —DISRUPTS→ Tubulin polymerization (GO:0007032); Tubulin polymerization (GO:0007032) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal migration (GO:0001705); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0002067); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Ptosis (HP:0000508); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Velopharyngeal dysfunction (HP:0000218); Neuronal migration (GO:0001705) —LEADS_TO→ Facial palsy, congenital (HP:0007310). Both MONDO:0012703 (characterized by cortical dysplasia) and MONDO:0060589 (characterized by facial palsy, ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction) are proposed to arise from haploinsufficiency of genes encoding tubulin subunits (TUBA1A and TUBB6). These mutations disrupt the fundamental process of tubulin polymerization, which is essential for the formation of microtubules. Impaired tubulin polymerization subsequently disrupts critical developmental pathways, most notably neuronal migration. Defects in neuronal migration can lead to structural abnormalities in the brain, manifesting as cortical dysplasia (MONDO:0012703). Furthermore, disruptions in neuronal development and function, stemming from the same underlying tubulin defects, can impact cranial nerve function and development, leading to phenotypes such as congenital facial palsy, ptosis, and velopharyngeal dysfunction (MONDO:0060589).
